replicated_directional_findings: Aomori remained strong relative to the batch average.
Kawasaki remained strong relative to the batch average.
Gifu remained weak relative to the batch average.
Yahiko remained weak relative to the batch average.
Exact 333.3m remained the weakest circumference group; first batch 1/11 top1, temporal replication 0/16 top1.
Exact 400m remained materially stronger than exact 333.3m in both batches.
Exact 335m remained intermediate and heterogeneous rather than collapsing or becoming uniformly strong.
non_claims: This does not justify live betting or automatic betting.
This does not justify subgroup retuning from these two batches alone.
This temporal replication is not fully independent-meeting replication because some races may be other days of the same meetings.

scientific_conclusion: The second preregistered 100-race batch replicates the existence and direction of substantial venue/circumference heterogeneity without retuning. Overall B1a ranking performance is better than batch 1 but still not uniformly strong. The strongest reproducible warning is exact 333.3m/Toyama weakness; 400m is materially more stable. Venue-specific operational rules still require a fully independent-meeting replication and larger-scale validation before adoption.
next_gate: Construct a fully independent-meeting historical replication set, then scale toward the existing ~2000-race substrate while preserving exact circumference, no-retune, no-odds-blocking and KR-015 evidence classification.
